key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Sudden, often during or after eating/drinking. LOCATION: RETROSTERNAL (midline chest behind breastbone). RADIATES to back occasionally. DURATION: Minutes, typically brief. CHARACTER: SQUEEZING, gripping, can mimic cardiac pain. AGGRAVATING: Swallowing (especially hot or cold liquids), eating. RELIEVING: Spontaneous resolution, nitroglycerin (can relieve, causing confusion with angina), calcium channel blockers. TIMING: Episodic, related to swallowing. SEVERITY: 5-8/10, can be severe. KEY POSITIVES: Dysphagia (difficulty swallowing), related to eating/drinking, relieved by nitrates (mimics angina!), no exertional pattern. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT exertional, NOT radiating to arm/jaw typically.

red_flags: New onset in elderly (rule out cardiac)
Weight loss or dysphagia to solids (suggests stricture/cancer)
